metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the fallback for a current id that accrues fewer than three (including zero) governed repository executions before the run ends, so the progress guarantee holds even when the model never gathers repository evidence for that id.
evidence: 'When the count reaches 3 and the id is still unbanked, the wrapper immediately invokes `fallback_record`'
'This same-response fallback is the progress guarantee: ... request exhaustion cannot leave that criterion at zero.'
Worked example assumes 'response steps 1, 2, and 3 each issue a parallel read/search batch' — it does not cover an id with fewer than three (or zero) governed repository executions.
findings.finding: The same-response fallback progress guarantee is gated exclusively on the current id's repository-execution counter reaching 3. The plan does not specify what happens to a current id that accrues zero governed repository executions before request exhaustion (e.g., the model relies only on prefetched evidence and never banks it, or exhausts the budget on other ids/text). Such an id's counter stays at 0, the fallback never fires, and it can reach recovery unbanked — the exact zero-progress state this repair targets.
findings.location: Repair design -> Wrapper state, composition, and progress guarantee; Worked example
scenarios: Model uses prefetched-evidence-first guidance, never issues a repository call for the current id, and never banks it before exhaustion
Budget exhausts while the current id's repository-execution counter is 1 or 2
findings.suggested_fix: State that a governed repository execution for the current id also fires the met=false fallback when it is the run's final governed action and the id is still unbanked, or add a run-end sweep that banks every still-unbanked policy id as provisional met=false.

findings.finding: The wrapper decision rule for a single model response that contains BOTH a record_criterion_verdict call and one-or-more repository evidence calls is not co-located/specified: it is unclear whether the record's bank-boundary advance is observed before or after the same-response evidence call is counted against and executed for the current id, which determines which id's counter the evidence step increments and whether a just-recorded id can still receive a step-3 fallback in the same response.
findings.location: Repair design -> Wrapper state, composition, and progress guarantee
findings.suggested_fix: Add a co-located rule: within one response, apply the record call's bank upsert (and boundary advance) FIRST under the shared lock, THEN recompute the current id from live banked_ids() before counting/executing that response's governed repository call — so a same-response record of id A moves the counter to the new current id and cannot trigger a fallback over A.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the COMMIT steering notice text (or its exact required intent tokens) so the parallel-same-response test has a pinned expected value and the LLM-facing steering wording is specified.
evidence: 'concurrent extras at that step receive a fixed COMMIT steering notice and do not execute'
Existing prior art has a fully-specified constant: TOOL_STEP_STEERING_NOTICE (agent_call.py:93-97).
findings.finding: The plan introduces a 'fixed COMMIT steering notice' returned to concurrent same-response repository calls but never defines its text/vocabulary, unlike the existing TOOL_STEP_STEERING_NOTICE which has a fixed, pinned string. Because the notice is emitted back to the model to steer it toward committing via record_criterion_verdict, its wording is part of the LLM-facing surface.
findings.location: Repair design -> Wrapper state, composition, and progress guarantee ('concurrent extras at that step receive a fixed COMMIT steering notice')
scenarios: Implementer must author the concurrent-extra notice string
Unit test for parallel same-response serialization asserts the notice content

evidence: 6 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: Reconcile the counter unit with the postcondition: state explicitly whether the third-response fallback counts governed RESPONSES (run steps) or REAL repository executions, and if the latter, specify how the completion layer distinguishes a memo cache hit from a wrapped-tool execution given it sits outside the memo layer.
evidence: Plan: 'Innermost to outermost composition is: existing step steering -> existing memo -> completion evidence policy -> existing runaway guard.'
Plan: 'After each first call returns, its unique run step is counted for the current id. When the count reaches 3 and the id is still unbanked, the wrapper immediately invokes fallback_record'
Plan postcondition: 'every first tool-origin bank occurs after at most three real repository executions'

src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py _memo_toolsets returns cached results (cache[sig] + nudge) for allowlisted read-only tools without invoking the wrapped tool, so a call routed through memo can complete without a real repository execution
findings.finding: The counting unit for the fallback (per-response / per-run_step, counted after each first governed call returns) does not equal the postcondition's unit ('three real repository executions'), because the completion layer is composed OUTSIDE the memo layer, so a memoized cache hit that performs no real repository work still increments the evidence-response counter.
findings.location: Repair design -> Wrapper state, composition, and progress guarantee; and Test contract postcondition
scenarios: Model re-reads the same file/search across three responses for one criterion; memo serves 2 of 3 from cache; the wrapper still counts 3 and forces met=false after only 1 real repository execution
A dense criterion whose evidence needs a genuine third distinct read is prematurely banked met=false because a cache-hit response consumed one of its three slots
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) redefine the postcondition to 'at most three governed evidence responses' to match the run-step counter, or (b) have the wrapped call return a signal (or place the completion layer inside memo) so only real repository executions increment the counter.

findings.checklist_item: Pin that the fallback write and the subsequent banked_ids()/current-id re-read happen inside the same shared-lock critical section using the live filesystem-backed banked_ids() (not a cached snapshot), so the just-written provisional entry is observed and the current-id boundary advances deterministically.
evidence: Plan: 'the wrapper immediately invokes fallback_record under the shared lock before returning the tool result, appends a notice naming that fail-closed bank, and advances through the live bank state.'
Plan: 'The current id is always the first criterion_ids entry absent from the live banked_ids() result; that observable bank transition is the reset boundary'

src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_banking.py banked_ids() -> set(self.all().keys()); all() re-globs and re-reads the bank directory from disk on every call (fresh read, so a preceding synchronous upsert write is visible)
findings.finding: The same-response fallback's read-your-own-write ordering is asserted but not pinned against banked_ids()'s filesystem-backed implementation: after fallback_record writes the provisional entry under the shared lock, the wrapper must 'advance through the live bank state', which requires banked_ids() to observe the just-written file before releasing the lock.
findings.location: Repair design -> Wrapper state, composition, and progress guarantee
scenarios: Fallback writes A/met=false, then the wrapper reads banked_ids() expecting A to be present so B becomes current; if the write-then-read ordering weren't synchronous the current-id would not advance and the same criterion could be re-counted

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the counter basis so the system-prompt 'third evidence response' and the wrapper's 'run_step with an executed governed repository tool' name the same counted event (or state explicitly that the wrapper counter is authoritative and the prompt wording is advisory only).
evidence: Model guidance: 'On the third evidence response, record `met=false` when the evidence has not demonstrated MET.'
Wrapper: 'After each first call returns, its unique run step is counted for the current id. When the count reaches 3 and the id is still unbanked, the wrapper immediately invokes `fallback_record`'
The wrapper counts only run_steps with an executed governed repository tool (evidence_tool_names = read_file/list_directory/search_files); a record-only or text-only response has no such execution.
findings.finding: The counter that drives the automatic met=false fallback is defined on two different, non-reconciled bases: the system-prompt rule counts 'evidence responses' while the wrapper counts run_steps at which a governed repository tool actually executed. A text-only response or a record-only response advances the model's notion of 'third evidence response' but not the wrapper counter (and vice versa), so the enforced boundary and the guidance boundary can fire at different response indices.
findings.location: Repair design -> Model guidance ('On the third evidence response, record met=false') vs. Wrapper state, composition, and progress guarantee ('its unique run step is counted for the current id. When the count reaches 3')
scenarios: Model issues a text-only reasoning turn between evidence batches
Model records a revision for an older id in a turn with no repository call for the current id
findings.suggested_fix: Define the counted unit once — 'a run_step at which at least one governed repository evidence tool executed for the current id' — and phrase the system-prompt guidance in those exact terms, noting that record-only/text-only responses do not advance the counter.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Capture the completion-wrapper composition ordering and the `_rebar_completion_evidence_policy` metadata contract in an ADR / AGENTS.md / design-doc update, and add it as an acceptance criterion.
evidence: 'A new substantive module owns the policy and wrapper'
'Innermost to outermost composition is: existing step steering -> existing memo -> completion evidence policy -> existing runaway guard.'
No acceptance criterion or step names an ADR/design-doc/AGENTS.md update capturing the ordering rationale or the _rebar_completion_evidence_policy metadata contract.
findings.finding: The new completion policy module introduces a novel wrapper-composition contract (a distinct completion evidence layer with a mandated innermost-to-outermost ordering: step steering -> memo -> completion policy -> runaway guard) but the plan does not capture this architectural decision in an ADR / AGENTS.md / design-doc update.
findings.location: Repair design -> Wrapper state, composition, and progress guarantee
scenarios: A future maintainer adds another toolset layer and reorders it relative to the completion layer, breaking the 'reject before memo/real tool' guarantee.
A future reader must reconstruct why the completion layer sits inside runaway rather than outside it.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC requiring a short design-note/ADR entry documenting the four-layer ordering invariant and the private metadata-attribute contract, co-located with the new module.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Instrument the fail-closed `fallback_record` path with an operator-visible log/metric (or a distinguishable marker) so a wrapper-forced provisional `met=false` is diagnosable and not conflated with a model-authored verdict.
evidence: 'fallback_record ... invokes the existing bound record_criterion_verdict callable for the named id as met=false, preserving its source="tool" vocabulary'
'appends a notice naming that fail-closed bank' — this notice is model-facing steering text, not an operator log/metric.
No AC or step instruments the fail-closed path with an operator-visible metric/log.
findings.finding: When the wrapper writes a provisional fail-closed `met=false` via `fallback_record`, the plan mandates preserving `source="tool"` vocabulary, making a wrapper-forced provisional verdict indistinguishable in the bank from a model-authored tool verdict; no operator-visible metric/log/trace surfaces that a fail-closed bank occurred.
findings.location: Repair design -> completion-only enforcement policy (`fallback_record`) and Wrapper progress guarantee
scenarios: An operator debugging a dense-run FAIL cannot tell whether a criterion failed on model judgment or was force-banked because evidence ran out at the third response.
A downstream consumer of the bank treats a provisional wrapper-forced false as an equal-authority model verdict.
findings.suggested_fix: Emit a structured log/counter when `fallback_record` fires (criterion id, response count), and add an AC asserting the fail-closed event is observable to operators without changing the persisted bank schema.
